{{Short description|Boolean algebra concept}}

In mathematics, '''Zhegalkin algebra''' is a set of [[Boolean functions]] defined by the nullary operation taking the value <math>1</math>, use of the binary operation of [[Logical conjunction|conjunction]] <math>\land</math>, and use of the [[Exclusive or|binary sum operation for modulo 2]] <math>\oplus</math>. The constant <math>0</math> is introduced as <math>1 \oplus 1 = 0</math>.<ref>[https://www.mathnet.ru/links/296149770c6a650e09ce139cb352ca3c/sm7400.pdf Zhegalkin, Ivan Ivanovich (1928). "The arithmetization of symbolic logic" (PDF). Matematicheskii Sbornik. 35 (3–4): 320. Retrieved 12 January 2024.], additional text.</ref> The negation operation is introduced by the relation <math>\neg x = x \oplus 1</math>. The disjunction operation follows from the identity <math>x \lor y = x \land y \oplus x \oplus y</math>.<ref name="Kap">Yu. V. Kapitonova, S.L. Krivoj, A. A. Letichevsky. ''Lectures on Discrete Mathematics''. — SPB., BHV-Petersburg, 2004. — ISBN 5-94157-546-7, p. 110-111.</ref>

Using Zhegalkin Algebra, any perfect disjunctive normal form can be uniquely converted into a [[Zhegalkin polynomial]] (via the Zhegalkin Theorem).

== Basic identities ==

* <math>x \land ( y \land z) = (x \land y) \land z</math>, <math>x \land  y = y \land x</math>
* <math>x \oplus ( y \oplus z) = (x \oplus y) \oplus z</math>, <math>x \oplus y = y \oplus x</math>
* <math>x \oplus x = 0</math>
* <math>x \oplus 0 = x</math>
* <math>x \land ( y \oplus z) = x \land y \oplus x \land z</math>

Thus, the basis of Boolean functions <math>\bigl\langle \wedge, \oplus, 1 \bigr\rangle</math> is [[Functional completeness|functionally complete.]]

Its inverse logical basis <math>\bigl\langle \lor, \odot, 0 \bigr\rangle</math> is also functionally complete, where <math>\odot</math> is the [[XNOR gate|inverse of the XOR operation]] (via [[Logical equality|equivalence]]).  For the inverse basis, the identities are inverse as well: <math>0 \odot 0 = 1</math> is the output of a constant, <math>\neg x = x \odot 0</math> is the output of the [[Negation|negation operation]], and <math>x \land y = x \lor y \odot x \odot y</math> is the [[Logical conjunction|conjunction operation]].

The functional completeness of the two bases follows from completeness of the basis <math>\{\neg, \land, \lor\}</math>.
